transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because even on my better days, I can’t shake the feeling that some people at church and in my walking club are watching me. It feels like they put little messages about me in the church bulletin, or in things they say.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?
Sometimes, when the house is quiet, I hear my name or a few words—like my friend calling from the kitchen or the porch. It sounds clear enough that I answer, and then I remember nobody's there.
Have you been struggling with persistent feelings of sadness, depression, or feeling down?
Yes. For most of this whole time, I’ve had this sadness in the background. I feel guilty a lot, and I just don’t have much interest in things, even when the other thoughts or the voices are quieter.
Have you ever experienced hearing voices or feeling watched during times when you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes. There was a few-week stretch where I was getting dressed, eating a little better, and didn’t feel so weighed down, but I still heard my name in the house. I still felt like people at church were hinting about me, too.
During those periods of sadness, did you feel down or depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

Yes. It was there most of the day, almost every day—just this sadness in the background, along with the guilt and not caring much about things. Even when the other things were quieter, that part didn’t really go away.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets diagnostic criteria for schizoaffective disorder, depressive type (F25.1). There is clear evidence of psychotic symptoms (ideas/delusions of reference and auditory hallucinations) co-occurring with a major depressive syndrome characterized by depressed mood, guilt, and pervasive anhedonia. Crucially, psychotic symptoms were explicitly reported to persist for a period of several weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, ruling out a purely mood-congruent psychotic depression (F32.3) and supporting a schizoaffective diagnosis.

confirmed_symptoms: Ideas/delusions of reference (feeling watched, believing messages are embedded in church bulletins)
Auditory hallucinations (hearing clear voices calling the patient's name when alone)
Depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day
Marked loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia)
